The Gambia launched its National Identity Management System on 30 June 2026 with instant issuance of the GAM ID, a pilot for selected institutions from 6 to 29 July and nationwide enrolment from 4 August, per the Ministry of Information.

President Barrow launched The Gambia's National Identity Management System (NIMS) and became its first enrollee, with GICTA describing it as the first national biometric-based digital identity platform.
President Barrow said ID cards will be integrated with civil registration and passport databases to create a unified digital ID system, and that digitalisation of national documents is in progress.
President Barrow referred to the existing National ID system run under a concession contract that the government will soon replace.

Public registration for the new biometric national ID card opened on 4 August 2026 in Greater Banjul under the National Identity Management System launched 30 June 2026, with phased expansion to other regions from 7 September 2026.
The government says the system combines a national identity register with biometric technology to reduce duplicate identities and fraud.

The Ministry for the Interior says the first phase of its contract with Margins ID Systems covers mass enrolment of citizens and residents on a new biometric ID system, replacing all valid cards free with ten-year cards.
The Ministry of Interior contracted a National Identity Management System and ICAO-compliant e-identity card infrastructure.
